app.name: Chaanbean
app.tagline: Credit checks and secured transactions for Indian businesses

subtitles.transactions: Deals the buyer accepts by OTP
subtitles.settlements: When the buyer pays in part

about.title: What ChaanBean does
points: Check a buyer before you give credit
Record the deal so the buyer agrees by OTP
Follow up and settle when payment is late

placeholder.body: This page is part of the Phase 1 build plan. The layout and navigation are final; the content arrives with Part {part}.

S01.title: Sign in
S01.purpose: Sign in or start sign-up with your mobile number and a one-time password.

S02.title: Verify your business
S02.purpose: Verify the business behind the account by GSTIN or PAN and create the organisation.

S03.title: Plans and checkout
S03.purpose: Choose Plan A, Plan B or pay-per-use, apply a coupon and pay.

S04.title: Dashboard
S04.purpose: Your credit exposure and what needs attention, with one-click entry to every action.

S05.title: Counterparties
S05.purpose: Find and manage every buyer, debtor and borrower, with risk and exposure at a glance.

S06.title: Add counterparty
S06.purpose: Register a buyer, debtor or borrower with verified identity and contact details.

S07.title: Counterparty profile
S07.purpose: Everything known about a counterparty: risk, reports, cases, transactions, documents and history.

S08.title: Credit Worthiness
S08.purpose: Choose which checks to run, see the price and plan balance of each, and which need consent.

S09.title: Check details and consent
S09.purpose: Give the identifiers the selected checks need and send the consent request.

S10.title: Consent request
S10.purpose: Review a request to view your business data and approve or decline it.

S11.title: Credit report
S11.purpose: All check results as one report with a risk band, a suggested credit range and the signals behind them.

S12.title: Case check
S12.purpose: Find court cases, FIRs and money laundering watchlist hits, and confirm which matches are real.

TXL.title: Business Security
TXL.purpose: Agreements your buyers accept by OTP, sealed as evidence.

S13.title: New agreement
S13.purpose: Create a seller-initiated, buyer-initiated or lender transaction with all terms the counterparty will accept.

S14.title: Review and send
S14.purpose: See the exact agreement the counterparty will see, and send it.

S15.title: Agreement
S15.purpose: Review an agreement and accept, reject or ask for changes.

S16.title: Agreement
S16.purpose: Track a transaction from draft to paid, record payments and get the evidence pack.

S17.title: New E-Settlement
S17.purpose: Record a settlement when a debtor agrees to pay, but not in full or not at once.

S18.title: Team and roles
S18.purpose: Manage who in your organisation can use Chaanbean and what they can do.

S19.title: Plan, usage and wallet
S19.purpose: Your wallet balance, plan, price list, ledger and invoices.

S20.title: Notification settings
S20.purpose: Choose how you are told about each event, and what counterparties see as the sender.

S21.title: Operations console
S21.purpose: Prices, plans, provider routing, organisations, consent records and audit search.

S22.title: Verify a document
S22.purpose: Confirm a Chaanbean agreement has not been altered since it was sealed.

items.q: Does my buyer need a ChaanBean account?
items.a: No. They get a link by WhatsApp, SMS or email and answer on their phone with an OTP.

items.q: Can I check a buyer without telling them?
items.a: Public checks like GST search, MSME and company records run without the buyer. GST turnover and CIBIL need the buyer's OTP consent, as the law requires.

items.q: What if a check finds nothing?
items.a: If the search ran and found no records (for example, no court cases), it is charged, because the search was done. If the source fails, nothing is charged.

items.q: Is an agreement accepted by OTP valid?
items.a: It is an electronic record with the buyer's name, mobile, OTP reference, time, IP address and device, sealed with a fingerprint. The evidence pack includes a draft certificate under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam for your lawyer.

items.q: How much credit should I give?
items.a: The report suggests a safe range of 1% to 2% of the buyer's last yearly turnover, less if turnover is falling, and none if the risk is High. It is a guide; the decision is yours.
Add money to your wallet, or buy a plan (the full plan payment goes into your wallet), by UPI, card or net banking. Your buyer pays you directly, as they do today.
